title: The Sunlight You See Is 8 Minutes Old
description: Light takes time to travel, so when you look at the Sun you are seeing it as it was about eight minutes ago.

scenes.text: The sunlight hitting your face right now left the Sun about eight minutes ago.
scenes.subject: sunrise
scenes.say: [whispers] The sunlight hitting your face right now... left the Sun about eight minutes ago.

scenes.text: The Sun is about one hundred and fifty million kilometers away. Even light needs time to cross that distance.
scenes.subject: sun
scenes.say: The Sun is about one hundred and fifty million kilometers away. Even light needs time to cross that distance.

scenes.text: Traveling at the speed of light, it takes around eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us.
scenes.subject: sun
scenes.say: Traveling at the speed of light, it takes around eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us.

scenes.text: So you always see the Sun as it was, not as it is. And for distant stars, that light can be thousands of years old.
scenes.say: [curious] So you always see the Sun as it was, not as it is. [gasps] And for distant stars, that light can be THOUSANDS of years old.

scenes.text: Every time you look up, you are looking back in time. Follow for more weird facts.
scenes.subject: sunset
scenes.say: [softly] Every time you look up, you are looking back in time. [chuckles] Follow for more weird facts.
